records.text: Dan Illouz called Tucker Carlson and Candace Owens intellectual vandals and an internal enemy whose ideas were being sold to Americans as patriotism.
records.speaker: Dan Illouz

appearances.snippet: I see a new enemy rising from within. ... I am speaking of a poison being sold to the American people as patriotism. I am speaking of the intellectual vandalism of Tucker Carlson and Candace Owens.

verification.notes: The transcript context shows Dan Illouz speaking from the Knesset lectern and calling Carlson and Owens a new enemy rising from within, describing a poison sold to Americans as patriotism, and naming their intellectual vandalism. The original recording contains the speech, while contemporaneous JTA/Washington Jewish Week and JNS reports independently reproduce those remarks and attribution. The statement accurately paraphrases Illouz's words and is verified as an attributed-speech claim, not as an endorsement of his characterization.

records.text: Dan Illouz said Tucker Carlson and Candace Owens resembled the woke left, attacked Western civilization, and expressed hatred of the West.
records.speaker: Dan Illouz

appearances.snippet: They claim to fight the woke left. They are no different than the woke left. ... Tucker Carlson tears down the legacy of Winston Churchill. ... Candace Owens says the roots of our faith are demonic. ... It is the same hatred of the West dressed up in a different costume.

verification.notes: The transcript context records Dan Illouz saying Carlson and Owens were no different from the woke left, contrasting attacks on Thomas Jefferson and Western civilization with Carlson's treatment of Churchill and Owens's description of faith roots as demonic, and concluding that it was the same hatred of the West in a different costume. The original recording contains the speech, and contemporaneous reports by JTA/Washington Jewish Week and Jewish Insider independently reproduce the relevant comparison and wording. The statement accurately summarizes Illouz's expressed opinion; verification concerns whether he said it, not whether the opinion is objectively correct.
